Rashi on Megillah 7a:10:1.hebrew: והלא כבר נאמר וידבר כו' - וקהלת כבר נאמרה, וכיון דלא כתב את כולן, למדת שמה שכתב — רוח הקודש היה:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:10:1.english: Wasn’t it already stated: “And he spoke,” etc. - And Ecclesiastes was already said [by him]; and since he did not write all of them [down], you have learned that what he wrote was [inspired by] the Holy Spirit.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:10:2.english: Do not add to his words - It is a verse in the Book of Proverbs.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:11:1.hebrew: דאי בעי כתב ואי בעי לא כתב - ולעולם מה שכתב משלות בעלמא נינהו, ולא מפי הקב"ה:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:11:1.english: That if he wished he wrote, and if he wished he did not write - And really, what he wrote were mere proverbs, and not from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:11:2.hebrew: תא שמע אל תוסף על דבריו - מדקאסר להוסיף עליהן, שמע מינה: ברוח הקודש נאמרו:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:11:2.english: Come and hear: Add you not unto his words - Since it forbids adding to them, learn from this that they were spoken through divine inspiration.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:12:1.hebrew: ויאמר המן בלבו - מנא ידעו כותבי המגילה שכך אמר בלבו? אלא, רוח הקודש נגלה עליהם:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:12:1.english: And Haman said in his heart - From where did the writers of the Megillah know that he said this in his heart? Rather, the Divine Spirit was revealed to them.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:13:1.hebrew: ויודע הדבר למרדכי - מי גלה לו? רוח הקדש שרה עליו:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:13:1.english: And the thing became known to Mordecai - Who revealed [it] to him? The Divine Spirit rested upon him.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:13:2.english: And on the plunder they did not lay their hands - How did they know what those far away did?

Rashi on Megillah 7a:15:1.hebrew: מפיש ואמר טובא - יביאו לבוש מלכות — אדעתא דנפשיה קאמר. שמע מינה, זאת היתה בלבו:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:15:1.english: He elaborated extensively and said - [When he said,] “Let royal apparel be brought,” he said [it] with himself in mind; deduce from this that this was in his heart.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:16:1.hebrew: נדמתה לו כאומתו - והיו אומרים בפיהם, זו משלנו היא:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:16:1.english: She appeared to him as [one of] his nation - And they would say with their mouths: “She is one of our own.”

Rashi on Megillah 7a:17:1.english: That of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba - [It is cited] later in our chapter.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:18:1.hebrew: פריסתקי שדור - שלוחים שלחו להם, למרדכי ואסתר, שלא נגענו בביזה, שלא ירע למלך:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:18:1.english: They dispatched messengers - They sent messengers to them, to Mordecai and Esther, [reporting:] “We did not touch the plunder, so that the king would not be displeased.”

Rashi on Megillah 7a:19:1.english: Shall not cease - From where did he know the future?

Rashi on Megillah 7a:20:2.hebrew: שתי מנות לאדם אחד - דכתיב: ״ומשלוח מנות איש לרעהו״ — שתי מנות לאדם אחד, ״ומתנות לאביונים״ — שתי מתנות לשני בני אדם. די לכל אחד ואחד מתנה אחת, דהא ״אביונים״ נמי תרתי משמע:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:20:2.english: Two portions to one person - As it is written: “And of sending portions one to another” — two portions to one person; “and gifts to the poor” — two gifts to two people. It is sufficient for each and every one [to receive] one gift, as “poor” also implies two.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:21:1.english: A third calf - The third of the womb.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:2:1.english: Ultimately they established it, etc. - And this is [what is meant by] “the second.”

Rashi on Megillah 7a:3:1.english: She sent to them - In the second year, to establish it upon them as an obligation.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:3:2.hebrew: קבעוני - ליום טוב ולקרייה, להיות לי לשם:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:3:2.english: Establish me - As a festival and for reading [the Megillah], to be a lasting name for me.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:3:3.english: You will arouse envy against us - For the nations will say that we rejoice in mentioning their downfall.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:3:4.english: I am already written - And there they will see what happened to them at the hands of Israel.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:4:1.english: Rav and Rav Ḥanina and Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rav Ḥaviva taught - [This refers to] that which we say below.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:4:2.hebrew: בכוליה סדר מועד - שהוזכרה שם זוג זה של ארבע חכמים הללו, חלופי רבי יוחנן ומכניסין רבי יונתן:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:4:2.english: Throughout the entire Order of Moed - [Wherever] this pair of these four Sages is mentioned there, exchange Rabbi Yoḥanan and insert Rabbi Yonatan.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:4:3.hebrew: שלישים - בשלשה מקומות יש לנו להזכיר מלחמת עמלק: בספר ואלה שמות (יז), ובמשנה תורה (כה), ובספר שמואל (א טו). וזהו שאמר שלמה: בדבר ששילשתו, אי אתה רשאי לרבעו:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:4:3.english: Three times - In three places we are to mention the war against Amalek: in the book of Exodus (17), in Deuteronomy (25), and in the book of Samuel (I 15). And this is what Solomon said: Regarding a matter that you have tripled, you are not permitted to quadruple it.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:5:1.english: “This,” that which is written here and in Deuteronomy - For everything that is written in the Torah, it calls [it] one writing.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:7:1.hebrew: אינה מטמאה את הידים - כשאר ספרים, דאמר ביציאות השבת (דף יד.) שגזרו עליהן לטמא את הידים לתרומה, ומחלוקת בית שמאי וב"ה היא:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:7:1.english: Does not render the hands ritually impure - [Unlike] other books, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Yetziot HaShabbat (page 14a), that they decreed upon them to render the hands impure for terumah; and it is a dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.

Rashi on Megillah 7a:9:1.hebrew: הוא דאמר כרבי יהושע - דאמר לעיל: "זאת" — מה שכתוב בתורה, "זכרון" — מה שכתוב במשנה תורה, "בספר" — מה שכתוב בנביאים. אבל במגילה לא ניתנה ליכתב, אלא לגורסה על פה ולקרותה:
Rashi on Megillah 7a:9:1.english: He stated [it] in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua - As [Rabbi Yehoshua] said above: “This” [is] what is written in the Torah, “a memorial” [is] what is written in Deuteronomy, “in the book” [is] what is written in the Prophets; but regarding the Megillah, it was not given to be written [as Scripture], but only to recite it orally and to read it.

Tosafot on Megillah 7a:15:1.hebrew: לכולהו איכא פירכא בר מדשמואל - וקשה: דלשמואל מי ליכא פירכא? דהא רבא גופיה הוא דאמר פרק רבי עקיבא (שבת דף פח. ושם) (מכאן מודעא רבה לאורייתא), שקבלו שנית בימי אחשורוש — אלמא דאיצטריך קרא לדרשא אחרינא! ויש לומר: דלא חשיב האי פירכא, דהא שפיר שמעינן מינה תרתי; ולא דמי האי פירכא לשאר פירכות דאינך, דסתר סברתם לגמרי:
Tosafot on Megillah 7a:15:1.english: “There is a refutation for all of them, except for that of Shmuel” - And it is difficult: As for Shmuel, is there really no refutation? For Rava himself said in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 88a, and there: “From here is a great notification [of coercion] regarding the Torah”) that they accepted [it] a second time in the days of Ahasuerus — evidently the verse was needed for another exposition! And one can say: He does not consider this a refutation, for we can well derive two [teachings] from it; and this refutation is not similar to the other refutations of the others, where he overturned their reasoning completely.

Tosafot on Megillah 7a:19:1.english: “And Rav Naḥman said from here: ‘Nor the memorial of them perish from their seed’” - For in the first clause of the verse, we see only the Jews of that generation.

Tosafot on Megillah 7a:8:1.hebrew: נאמרה לקרות ולא לכתוב - משמע דסבר דמותר לקרותה ע"פ. וקשה, דהיכי פליג על סתם משנה דלקמן דפ"ב (דף יז:), דתני: "קראה על פה — לא יצא"? ורב נמי הוא דאמר לקמן (מגילה דף יט.) שצריך לכותבה ולתופר' בגידין, ור' יוחנן נמי [אמר] (שם:) דאם קראה בין הכתובים לא יצא! לכך נר' לפר', דהא דקאמר לא ניתנה ליכתב — ברוח הקודש, אבל מדרבנן ניתנה ליכתב ולקרות. ואכתי קשיא, דהא אמרינן בפ' הממונה במסכת יומא (דף כט.): "נמשלה אסתר לאילת השחר, מה שחר סוף הלילה, אף אסתר סוף הנסים". ופריך: "והא איכא חנוכה?" ומשני: "ניתן ליכתב קאמר". ופריך: "הניחא למאן דאמר ניתן ליכתב, אלא למאן דאמר לא ניתן ליכתב, מאי איכא למימר?" ואין לומר דהא דניתן ליכתב — מדרבנן קרי כתיבה, דאם כן הדרא קושיין לדוכתא: דהא איכא חנוכה, שניתנה לכתוב מדרבנן במגילת תענית! ותירץ הר"ר אלחנן, דכתיבה דמגילה מהניא טפי, דהא צריכה גידין ושרטוט וכמה דברים דלא צריכי במגילת תענית:
Tosafot on Megillah 7a:8:1.english: "It was stated to be read and not to be written" - This implies that he maintains that it is permitted to read it by heart. And this is difficult, for how could he disagree with an anonymous Mishnah later in chapter 2 (17b), which teaches: "[If] one read it by heart, he has not fulfilled [his obligation]"? And Rav also is the one who said later (Megillah 19a) that it is necessary to write it and sew it with sinews; and Rabbi Yochanan also [said] (there) that if one read it among the Ketuvim (Writings), he has not fulfilled [his obligation]! Therefore, it seems [correct] to explain that this which was said, "it was not given to be written," [means it was not given] through the Divine Spirit, but by Rabbinic decree it was given to be written and to be read. Yet it is still difficult, for behold, we say in the chapter [entitled] Hamemuneh in Tractate Yoma (29a): "Esther was compared to the dawn; just as the dawn is the end of the night, so too Esther was the end of the miracles." And [the Gemara there] objects: "But isn't there Hanukkah?" And it answers: "He said [this regarding a miracle that] was permitted to be written." And it objects: "This works well according to the one who says [it] was permitted to be written; but according to the one who says [it] was not permitted to be written, what can be said?" And one cannot say that this [status of being] permitted to be written by Rabbinic decree is called "writing" — for if so, our objection returns to its place: for behold, there is Hanukkah, which was permitted to be written by Rabbinic decree in Megillat Taanit! And Rabbeinu Rabbi Elchanan answered that the writing of the Megillah is more significant, as it requires sinews [for stitching] and scoring [of lines], and several things that are not required for Megillat Taanit.
